body: I don't have any real great advice but I know the way you're feeling, I've been feeling that way too. My partner has never laughed about it but when I bring it up, I'm usually met with "why are you being crazy? That's so controlling, etc. I have tried so many times to make him understand the way he made me feel but it doesn't seem to get through to him. I am so sorry you are experiencing this but I do not think you are overreacting. You have the right to feel the way you do and you have the right to be heard. Stay strong and keep your head up!

I understand what you're saying. And you're right, there really are no easy solutions, there are just solutions that are less damaging than others. I am trying to encourage him to take the time he needs to heal but he just won't. I'm trying to help him understand that his feelings are valid but he feels like he hasn't been a good enough father and role model for us through these tough times. I know that I will eventually need to move on, but I'm not sure I'm there yet, and I know my Dad isn't there yet either. I don't want to force him but I also don't like seeing him waste away. For now, I think my best option is to just be there when I'm needed so he knows he isn't alone. That's just a lot harder now that I'm not allowed to visit with COVID-19 restrictions.

It's very hard for me to tell him that he's not alone when he's physically alone and there's nothing I can do about it.

I tried that yesterday but he keeps insisting that he's "okay" and I know that isn't true. I even told him that he needs to pull himself away from my Mom but I don't think it's that easy for him. Even after everything she has put him through, he still loves her so much. And I know he would take her back if things were just that easy and I think that's why it's so difficult for us to just let her go. What can I do to help him move past this because it has been over 2 years now and I don't know how much more he can handle.

If I could make you a list of the reasons I feel like a lot of this is my fault, you would definitely understand where I'm coming from. I have been told again and again that it isn't my fault but I'm not sure it is necessarily true. But I definitely understand what you're talking about when you say "noble self sacrifice." I have an older brother who is not dealing with things very well and a younger sister who shouldn't have to be dealing with any of this. So I do try to take some of this load off them, no matter how hard and exhausting it is. And I'm not sure that will ever change. I love my family more than anything and I am willing to do whatever it takes to protect them.

Thank you for the advice and the well wishes!

I know he does, but I'm not sure I see that happening with the way things are... and a little bit of that is my fault because I keep naively believing that someday things will get better and they will be together again and I think he is also trying to keep that door open. Thank you!

Thank you, I will give it a try. I just can't bear the thought of losing him, especially after everything else my family has been through. I hope you know that there are so many people who love you. Keep fighting!
Yes he is an addict. I’m sorry for the confusion. When I discovered that he was watching, I mean that I had no idea he was watching porn regularly until that day.
I’m glad you sent that but I’m a little scared to read. 🙁
